---
title: "3. Transient analysis"
subtitle: "Follow an RC circuit through time"
julia:
  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../.."]
---

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate("../..")
using Amber
```

Transient analysis solves the circuit's differential equations. Sources may
carry a waveform, and capacitors and inductors retain dynamic state.

```{julia}
@circuit RCStep(; R=10kΩ, C=10nF) begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    output = node()
    Source = voltage_source(
        input,
        gnd;
        dc=0V,
        waveform=Step(low=0V, high=1V, at=100μs, rise=1μs),
    )
    R1 = resistor(input, output; value=R)
    C1 = capacitor(output, gnd; value=C)
    observe(voltage(input), voltage(output), current(C1))
end

circuit = RCStep();
result = transient(circuit, 0s => 600μs; saveat=2μs, max_step=2μs);
```

The interval is written as a Julia pair, `start => stop`. `saveat` controls the
returned sample grid; `max_step` limits how far the integrator may advance.

## Work with traces

```{julia}
time = result.axis
input_voltage = voltage(result, :input)
output_voltage = voltage(result, :output)

@assert length(time) == length(output_voltage)
(first(time), last(time), output_voltage[end])
```

For an ideal RC step beginning at $t_0$, the response is

$$
V_{out}(t)=V_{step}\left(1-e^{-(t-t_0)/(RC)}\right).
$$

Compare the simulated point one time constant after the step:

```{julia}
τ = 10kΩ * 10nF
target_time = 100μs + τ
index = argmin(abs.(time .- target_time))
expected = 1V * (1 - exp(-1))

(time=time[index], simulated=output_voltage[index], expected)
```

## Trust, but verify

```{julia}
result.stats[:converged]
get(result.stats, :rejected_steps, 0)
result.stats[:warnings]
```

Reduce `max_step` and compare a measurement when sharp edges or fast nonlinear
events matter. A dense output plot does not by itself prove time-step
convergence.
